description.from:
Record of intent for a local embedding/semantic-search store for BotSpy session data. Record only; nothing here is committed to Cargo or code yet.

## 1. Relational store: SQLite

In-process, single-file, no server. Rust bindings via rusqlite or sqlx. macOS has shipped SQLite in the system frameworks since 10.4, so a Swift Mac app can share the same database file. WAL mode for concurrent readers and writers, so an out-of-process scanner CLI can write while the app reads.

## 2. Vector search: sqlite-vec

An extension living in the same SQLite file. Brute-force cosine similarity, which is fine for thousands of session embeddings.

## 3. Embedding model: all-MiniLM-L6-v2

Distilled BERT, 6 layers, 384-dim vectors (~1.5 KB each), ~80 MB quantized, open weights. OPEN QUESTION (deployment): bundle the weights vs fetch on first launch.

## 4. Runners

The Rust side uses candle, tract (ONNX), or burn. The Swift/Mac side uses MLX (mature bindings, mlx-community conversions). There are no first-class Rust MLX bindings, so Rust shells out or uses ONNX, and MLX lives in the Swift layer.

## 5. Core design rule: one model, one set of weights

The ONNX export and the MLX conversion must produce bit-identical vectors, so the store doesn't care which side did the embedding.

## 6. Performance targets

Query embedding under 100 ms on MLX (Apple Silicon), 50–200 ms on CPU via tract. Scanner batch embedding is where MLX GPU batching earns its keep (seconds vs minutes).

## Open questions

- Bundle the weights vs fetch on first launch.
- How bit-identical vectors across ONNX/tract and MLX will be verified. Floating-point kernels usually differ slightly, so a golden-vector test with an exact or tolerance-based comparison is TBD; Ryan decides.

## Milestones as Kanbus epics

Each milestone of this initiative is represented as an epic in Kanbus, created under this initiative on the BotSpy board. Proposed milestones (future epics), NOT yet created:

- SQLite store with WAL mode
- sqlite-vec vector search
- MiniLM embedding via Rust ONNX/tract
- Swift/MLX embedding with a cross-runner vector-parity check
- Scanner batch embedding

## 1. Relational store: SQLite

In-process, single-file, no server. Rust bindings via rusqlite or sqlx. macOS has shipped SQLite in the system frameworks since 10.4, so a Swift Mac app can share the same database file. WAL mode for concurrent readers and writers, so an out-of-process scanner CLI can write while the app reads.

## 3. Embedding model: all-MiniLM-L6-v2

Distilled BERT, 6 layers, 384-dim vectors (~1.5 KB each), ~80 MB quantized, open weights. OPEN QUESTION (deployment): bundle the weights vs fetch on first launch.

## 4. Runners: tract (ONNX) on CPU

tract (ONNX) on CPU, one engine for every consumer. A Swift Mac app still shares the same SQLite file but does not embed with MLX.

## 5. Core design rule: one model, one set of weights, one engine

One model, one set of weights, one engine (ONNX/tract), so vectors are consistent by construction.

## 6. Performance targets

Query embedding 50–200 ms on CPU via tract. Scanner batch embedding runs on CPU (no GPU path).

## Open questions

- Bundle the weights vs fetch on first launch.

## Milestones as Kanbus epics

Each milestone of this initiative is represented as an epic in Kanbus, created under this initiative on the BotSpy board. Proposed milestones (future epics), NOT yet created:

- SQLite store with WAL mode
- sqlite-vec vector search
- MiniLM embedding via ONNX/tract
- Scanner batch embedding (CPU)
